title: For the first time, police taser works
article: Police have effectively used a taser gun for the first time since the weapons were added to the force's arsenal two months ago.
Officers used a taser to incapacitate a knife-wielding man during a domestic dispute at a south side home Saturday night.
The taser fired two tiny darts connected by a wire, which stuck to the man, emitting a 65,000- volt charge that froze his body.
Both darts must make contact for the taser to work.
Police first tried to talk the man into surrendering the knife.
They also pepper-sprayed him but it had little effect.
Police spokesman Dean Parthenis said tasers have only been deployed in four other cases.
On May 16, a tactical officer tried to use a taser to control a drunk man wielding a butcher knife, but only one dart connected with the man.
Minutes later, the officer used his handgun and fatally shot John Pavic, who had lunged at him with the knife.
In the remaining cases, Parthenis said the suspects surrendered when officers threatened to use their tasers.
"The taser acts as a strong deterrent either way," he said.
The force ordered 21 tasers at $600 each in March, after a year- long trial.
They were distributed to four city divisions for use on the streets in May.
